name: Escanor
role: A stationary attacker adapted from Escanor's Rhitta axe slash and Sunshine. All values and mechanics are Tower Defense proposals, not claims about canon execution.
weakness: The unit does not model time of day, Escanor's transformation, or Sunshine's rise and fall. Its attacks require a clear path, and its temporary boost affects only its own attack.

sourceFacts.quote: Super Slash「微塵斬りスーパースラッシュ, Sūpā Surasshu; lit.
"Atomic Slash"」: Escanor delivers a powerful downwards slash with his axe that causes considerable damage that can be felt from several meters away.
It is incredibly heavy and most of its weight is concentrated on the head, which makes it very off-balanced yet, during the day, Escanor is able to wield it with one hand.

His incredible brute strength increases in conjunction with his magical power, as a single swing from his axe Rhitta upon transforming, was enough to cleave Galand in two and swing it with a single arm whereas Galand has a hard time even moving it with two.
Sunshine: Cruel Sun「無慈悲な太陽クルーエル・サン, Kurūeru San; lit.
"Merciless Sun"」: Escanor creates a miniature Sun, which radiates so much heat that it melts nearby armor.
He can control it with hand gestures and strike his opponents with it, and it will increase in size.
Escanor is able to imbue Rhitta with his magic, which causes the slashes from his axe to also burn his foes.
Sunshine: At high noon, Escanor reaches his absolute peak and becomes The One, "the invincible incarnation of power", according to Merlin.
This form only lasts for one minute.
While in this form, Escanor's strength increases to the point where with a single strike of his hand, he could knock off Meliodas in his Assault Mode.
The One「天上天下唯我独尊ザ・ワン, Za Wan; lit.
"Vainglorious Existence across Heaven and Earth"」: During noon, when his power is at its peak, for one minute he becomes the manifestation of power itself and his body dwarfs normal people.
Sunshine: Crazy Prominence「爆発する矜持クレイジー・プロミネンス, Kureijī Purominensu; lit.
"Exploding Arrogance"」: Escanor produces a large amount of miniature suns from his body that explode on impact.

path1.name: Cruel Sun
path1.theme: Choose this path for heat that persists on hit and later affects nearby enemies, while keeping Escanor's selected-target axe attack.
path1.rationale: Choose this path for heat that persists on hit and later affects nearby enemies, while keeping Escanor's selected-target axe attack.

path2.name: The One
path2.theme: Choose this path for a permanent increase in striking speed that culminates in a temporary, manually triggered The One attack boost.
path2.rationale: Choose this path for a permanent increase in striking speed that culminates in a temporary, manually triggered The One attack boost.

path3.name: Crazy Prominence
path3.theme: Choose this path to turn selected-target attacks into a volley whose separate impacts can reach nearby enemies.
path3.rationale: Choose this path to turn selected-target attacks into a volley whose separate impacts can reach nearby enemies.

proposedMechanics.name: Many Miniature Suns
proposedMechanics.effect: On a volley hit, adapt Crazy Prominence's many miniature suns as the attack's bounded volley; each projectile can produce the defined impact splash. This does not create independent actors or additional attacks beyond the volley.

proposals.name: Sunshine's daylight cycle
proposals.reason: The Definition has no time-of-day schedule that gradually raises Escanor's power toward noon and then reduces it after sunset.

proposals.name: Pride Flare's lake vaporization
proposals.reason: The Definition has no instant, lake-scale environmental destruction mechanic.

proposals.name: Rhitta heat storage and release
proposals.reason: The Definition has no heat-storage resource or command-triggered release mechanic.

reservedTechniques.name: Pride Flare
reservedTechniques.reason: Its instant lake-scale environmental destruction is not represented by the bounded attack mechanics.

reservedTechniques.name: Final Prominence
reservedTechniques.reason: The distinct gigantic swirling fireball technique is not selected; the volley is a separate bounded adaptation.
